query: Under contemporary Swiss case law, when is a contractual non-compete clause (Konkurrenzklausel / clause de non-concurrence) valid and enforceable against a former employee?

audited_product_bundle.query: Under contemporary Swiss case law, when is a contractual non-compete clause (Konkurrenzklausel / clause de non-concurrence) valid and enforceable against a former employee?
query_variants: non-compete clause Swiss Federal Supreme Court requirements

answer.prose: A non‑compete clause is valid and enforceable only if it is limited in time, space and content and is justified by a protectable interest of the employer that remains proportional to the employee’s actual activity; a two‑year duration is generally acceptable when trade‑secret protection is at issue [CH‑2020‑FR‑001]. Generic clauses that cover all employees irrespective of real competition risk violate proportionality and are invalid, the decisive factor being the employee’s concrete function and access to customer data [CH‑2019‑DE‑014]. The clause is also unenforceable if the employer waives the compensation due during the notice period, since retroactive cure is excluded [CH‑2021‑DE‑042]. Moreover, the clause cannot be invoked against an employee who had no access to confidential information; the employer must prove a concrete risk of actual competition [CH‑2022‑IT‑007]. The old approach that allowed a clause based solely on the employer’s protectable interest without a strict proportionality test has been abandoned by recent jurisprudence [CH‑2016‑FR‑088]. Finally, non‑compete clauses are not permissible in apprenticeship relationships, where the apprentice’s interest in acquiring skills outweighs the employer’s economic interest [CH‑2018‑DE‑031].
